Specifically, the `content` dictionary inside `additional_response` is shared across all routes when defined at the app level. When `deep_dict_update` is used to add the schema to this `content` dictionary, it modifies the original object, leading to cumulative duplication of the `anyOf` references.

steps.message:
I fixed the issue where app-level responses with both a `model` (especially `Union` types) and `content` were causing duplicate `$ref` entries in the generated OpenAPI schema.

The root cause was a shallow copy (`.copy()`) of the response definition in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`. Because the `content` dictionary was shared across all routes, modifications made during the OpenAPI schema generation for one route were leaking into others, causing the `anyOf` list to grow cumulatively.

I changed `process_response = additional_response.copy()` to `process_response = copy.deepcopy(additional_response)` in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py` to ensure each route works with its own independent copy of the response configuration.

To verify, you can run the reproduction script `repro.py` (or a similar test case defining app-level `responses` with `model` as a `Union` and specified `content`).

steps.message:
The issue was that app-level responses with both a `model` (specifically a `Union` of Pydantic models) and `content` caused duplicate `$ref` entries in the generated OpenAPI schema because `additional_response` was being shallow-copied, leading to shared state across routes. I have verified that changing `process_response = additional_response.copy()` to `process_response = copy.deepcopy(additional_response)` in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py` fixes this behavior.

The fix has been verified with a reproduction script.
